The page describes no territory and gives no infobox figures; Cliopatria's Papal States shape of 1849 (about 39,300 km2) is used as the outline, which overstates a republic whose hold on the Legations and the Marche is not documented on the page. region.text: the Papal States of 1849, which the Republic claimed after the Pope's flight to Gaeta (the page describes no territory)

ledger.note: 9 February 1849: the Roman Republic is proclaimed. The Constituent Assembly 'proclaimed the Roman Republic after midnight on 9 February' after Pius IX left Rome on the night of 24 November 1848 for Gaeta; the elections had been held on 21 January 1849. The territory is the researcher's reading of 'the Papal States'; the page gives none.

region.text: Civitavecchia, where the French landed, and Rome, which they besieged

ledger.note: 25 April 1849: the French land at Civitavecchia to restore the Pope. 'some eight to ten thousand French troops under General Charles Oudinot landed at Civitavecchia'; Garibaldi entered Rome on 27 April and the French were beaten back on 30 April. The siege began 'in earnest' on 1 June.

region.text: Civitavecchia, where the French landed, and Rome, which they besieged

ledger.note: 3 July 1849: the French enter Rome. 'the French prevailed on 29 June'; a truce was negotiated on 1 July; Garibaldi withdrew with about 4,000 men to San Marino on 2 July; 'The French Army entered Rome on 3 July and reestablished the Holy See's temporal power.'

ledger.note: 3 July 1849: the Roman Republic falls and papal rule is restored (the pope returned to Rome only in April 1850). The page dates the French entry, not the dissolution; the Assembly debated three options on 30 June.

region.text: the Papal States of 1849, which the Republic claimed after the Pope's flight to Gaeta (the page describes no territory)

ledger.note: July 1849: the Roman Republic ends after about five months. The Triumvirate of Armellini, Mazzini and Saffi had been proclaimed on 22 March 1849 when news of Novara arrived.

wars.name: Siege of Rome (1849)

zones.text: Civitavecchia, where the French landed, and Rome, which they besieged

wars.outcome: French troops under Oudinot landed at Civitavecchia on 25 April 1849, besieged Rome from 1 June, prevailed on 29 June and entered the city on 3 July, restoring the Pope's temporal power; Neapolitan troops also 'entered Roman Republic territory' and Spain sent 4,000 men to Gaeta, both undated on the page.

certainty.note: The page names no territory; only Rome and Civitavecchia are placed. The Republic's real hold on the provinces is not documented here.

sources.title: Roman Republic (1849)

notes: New rebel dossier, a state Cliopatria lacks; the papal-states dossier already carries the 9 February loss and 3 July gain against the slug 'roman-republic-1849', and reviews the Papal States shape of 1849 as 'ok'. One page opened (budget). The page gives no territory, area or dissolution date, so the Papal States shape is the outline and the dissolve is dated by the French entry (3 July; some sources say 4 July). The Austrian occupation of Bologna, Ferrara and Ancona (May-June 1849) and the Neapolitan advance (19 May) are not on the page and are not in the ledger; they are a gap for a reviewer with the Papal States page. Type 'rebel' (hatched) because the Republic was crushed by the French within five months.
